Samira — thanks for the details and the attachment. Cleared it with product and infra; below are three pragmatic reservation options with a one-page summary for procurement. I aimed to balance your latency target, predictable unit cost, and an aggressive procurement timeline.

Option A — Pilot Sprint (lowest friction)- Minimum footprint: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved)- Purpose: validate end-to-end routing, KV warmups, and prefix cache sizing with production traffic- Ramp schedule: immediate activation, 2–4 week validation, then either decommit or step to Option B- Burst: access to hosted burst pool up to +16 GPUs for short windows (subject to availability)- Good when you need fast launch and low upfront commit

Option B — Production Foundation (recommended starter)- Minimum footprint: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved baseline)- Purpose: sustained 95th pct latency under expected traffic with room for autoscaling headroom- Ramp schedule: T0 activate 24 GPUs, T+30 days evaluate (metrics review), T+60 days scale to 40 GPUs if utilization > 70% during peak- Burst: warm-standby cross-region (cold-standby in EU) with automated failover policy- Includes 2 weeks of migration and warm-cache tuning with engineering support

Option C — Growth Commitment (predictable unit economics)- Minimum footprint: 64 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved baseline) with staged increase to 128 over 90 days- Purpose: supports aggressive growth and sustained heavy peak windows; lower per-token unit cost- Ramp schedule: start 64 GPUs, +32 GPUs at T+30, +32 GPUs at T+60, +GOG (graceful overprovision) at T+90 based on observed throughput- SLA: 99.95% uptime SLA and dedicated on-call for first 90 days

Operational notes (applies to all options):- GPU equivalence: we size around A100-80GB equivalents; we can provide alternate sizing for B/Tr4/8s if you prefer lower power/quantized variants- Batching & KV cache: we recommend early work on request shaping to maximize batching and prefix cache reuse — this reduces needed GPU count by ~15–30% depending on model & sequence length- Failover: automated model-variant fallback to smaller quantized variants for capacity shortfalls- Contract flexibility: step-up windows every 30 days; decommit after 90 days with 30-day notice for Options B/C

I attached a short capacity estimate (redwood_capacity_estimate.pdf) and a procurement-ready one-page matrix. If this looks good I can convert Option B into a line-item reserved offer (inc. pricing) for your procurement team.

Next steps suggested: 1) confirm preferred option by Sep 30; 2) we send a line-item reserved offer + SOW; 3) PO by Oct 10; 4) onboarding kickoff week of Oct 18.

Thanks — Neha

Hi Samira / Neha — quick technical note from infra:

1) GPU equivalency and batch windows: your model profiling shows a mix of medium-length sequences. For stable 180ms P95 at peak QPS, 24 A100-eq GPUs is a realistic sustained baseline if we aggressively optimize batching and KV cache reuse. The main risk is cold cache on burst spikes — that's where staged ramp and warm-cache credits matter.

2) Minimum recommendation for your two-phase path: start with 24 GPUs (T0) for 90 days, then add 40 GPUs (to reach 64) over 60 days. We recommend an intermediate autoscale buffer of 8 GPUs (hot-swap) to handle short-term spikes during the scale window.

3) Warm-standby (same-region) vs cross-region: warm-standby within the same country typically costs ~12–18% premium on baseline reserved spend (region-specific network + reserved buffer), cross-country raises that to ~25% given egress and redundancy. We can provide exact deltas for the US regions once you pick target AZ/region.

4) Credits: we can offer a 2-week warmup credit (apply to compute usage) and 1-week migration support at no extra cost for commitments >= 64 GPUs. For the 24->64 two-phase path we can extend a one-time 10% compute credit for the first billing cycle during the scale event.

I can attach a short technical appendix if you want measured throughput curves for your model traces.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
